key_insight: Calculated reaction rates identify methyl adsorption at surface radical sites as the strongest methyl-depletion pathway and reveal direction-dependent migration on hydrogen-terminated diamond.
engineering_relevance: These rate coefficients help connect atomic-scale surface chemistry to larger-scale models of chemical vapor deposition diamond growth.
method: Combine density functional theory with variational transition state theory.
Calculate methyl adsorption, desorption and migration rates, including barrierless reactions.
Treat quasi-free methyl rotation explicitly to improve vibrational partition functions.
evidence_signal: Theoretical rate calculations for the (100)-(2×1):H diamond surface support dominant radical-site adsorption and anisotropic methyl migration; the abstract reports no experimental validation.
watch_item: Predicting overall growth rates requires additional hydrogen and other gas–surface reaction data; this study uses physics-based calculations, not AI.
paper_title: Methyl radicals dynamics on (100)--(2x1):H diamond surfaces based on refined variational transition state calculations of gas-surface reaction rate coefficients
